facts.claim: Any potential benefit it may have offered has been eclipsed by its role in Coalition/Conservative government social welfare policies that have blamed the victim and justified restriction of entitlements.

facts.claim: Activity in the insula/somatosensory cortex correlated with the belief in a just world.
facts.quote: FMRI results revealed an activation of dorsal ACC, RTPJ, and insula when perceiving norm violations, but only activity in insula/somatosensory cortex correlated with the belief in a just world.

research.angle: While just-world views are linked to extremist attitudes and specific brain activity, empathy for victims can reduce the tendency to blame them.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that just-world beliefs are linked to extremist attitudes and specific brain regions, and that government models have been used to justify victim-blaming in welfare policy.
research.caveat: The research on empathy and victim-blaming is specific to sexual harassment and does not necessarily generalize to all types of misfortunes.
